title: Vector service anomaly scratch log - Mika
content:
Quick notes / breadcrumb trail for the vector embedding + rerank endpoint anomaly (dimension mismatch errors + p99 latency spike). Personal scratchpad — not polished.

Summary of what I observed:
- Around 2026-03-04 02:10 UTC we saw a sudden increase in 503s and ValueError dimension mismatch exceptions from the reranker path. At the same time p99 latency for /v1/rerank jumped from ~60ms to ~420ms for a subset of requests.
- Impact: a handful of customer accounts (small traffic) hit degraded UX; automated rollbacks to model-v1 didn't fully recover latency.

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-03-04 01:48 UTC: Canary rollout started for model variant 'openvec-1536-q4' (PR #4123). Canary config: 5% traffic route to new variant for embeddings service via routing policy.
- 2026-03-04 02:05 UTC: Alerts for rerank p99 rising (Grafana alert).
- 2026-03-04 02:10 UTC: First customer Slack reports of search re-ranking timeouts.
- 2026-03-04 02:12 UTC: Observed repeated 'DimensionMismatch: expected 1024 got 1536' from the rerank microservice logs.
- 2026-03-04 02:20 UTC: Scaled up dedicated pool as a mitigation (manual). Latency improved slightly but errors persisted.
- 2026-03-04 03:00 UTC: Rolled back canary to 0% for openvec-1536-q4; traffic back to stable. 503s decreased, but p99 still elevated for ~30 min for cached sessions.

Reproduction steps I ran locally (notes):
- Minimal script that calls embeddings endpoint then rerank pipeline sequentially; reproduce mismatch when mixing model variants.
Command: 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"openvec-1536-q4","input":["test doc"]}' | jq -r '.data[0].embedding | length'
  # returns 1536

  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rerank-1024","query_embedding": <embedding-from-above>, "candidates": [...] }'
  # error: ValueError: input embedding dimension 1536 != expected 1024

- Local hypothesis: some requests were being embedded by the canary model (1536 dims) while rerank service expected 1024 dims from stable. The routing policy should have pinned request flow, but there was a mismatch in header propagation (x-redwood-model-id) causing cross-variant mixing.

Key error snippets (from service logs):
- reranker-3bbf: ERROR ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536 at rerank/handler.py:238
- emb-proxy: WARN unknown-model-variant fallback to openvec-1536-q4 for user/1234 (should have been pinned to openvec-1024)
- autoscaler: INFO downscaling pool 'embeddings-eu' triggered at 02:08 UTC — weird given spike; suspect race with warmup.

Latency numbers (sample from APM traces):
- baseline p50: 28ms, p95: 82ms, p99 pre-incident: 60ms
- during incident p50: 70ms, p95: 260ms, p99: 420ms
- median tokenization time increased ~2x for some requests (tokenizer container saturated).

Hypotheses / possible causes:
1) Model dimension mismatch from rolling canary: embeddings produced 1536-d vectors while downstream reranker was compiled for 1024 — missing compatibility check in routing layer.
2) Embedding proxy cache TTL or edge sticky routing misapplied; some requests for same session hit different model variants (cache key didn't include model id).
3) Autoscaler downsized some warm pods leading to CPU spikes on remaining pods causing tokenization latency, which cascaded into rerank timeouts.
4) Quantized kernel selection (q4 path) on newer variant triggers slower CPU fallback for certain lengths (regression in kernel fallback path).

Quick experiments tried (results):
- Force both endpoints to explicit model_v=1024 in request headers -> no dimension errors, latency normal for test load. (Suggests routing/header bug).
- Replayed trace volume with pinned model ids -> no spikes.
- Deployed quick check that validates embedding dim at proxy and short-circuits request with 400 + helpful message -> prevented downstream exception but is a band-aid.

Notes on instrumentation gaps I noticed:
- Routing logs don't consistently emit model-id for every request; adds difficulty correlating which requests hit which variant.
- Rerank microservice traces don't record embedding length as a span tag (should add for future incidents).
- No alert for dimension-mismatch exceptions specifically — only 5xx alert.

Immediate next steps (what I plan to do / suggested):
- Add a short-term routing guard: enforce model compatibility at proxy (validate embedding length against reranker expected length) and return 400 with guidance. (WIP PR idea).
- Add span tags: embedding_dim, model_variant_id for emb and rerank services. Low-risk changelist.
- Fix routing policy to include model_id in sticky cookie/cache key; verify canonicalization of model ids.
- Add Grafana panel for dimension-mismatch exception rate.
- Postmortem: gather list of affected customers, timeline, and mitigation steps; coordinate with CS.

TODO (personal):
- [ ] Run full traffic replay for last 6 hours around incident to see exact percent of mixed-variant flows.
- [ ] Add unit test in router that asserts cache key contains model id.
- [ ] Follow-up with release-engineering: confirm canary rollout config was applied correctly for PR #4123.
- [ ] Add doc snippet to runbook about embedding-dim mismatch and how to triage quickly (error messages, mitigation).

Open questions / TODOs for team:
- Why did rollback not immediately restore p99? (warmup / cache propagation?)
- Did any customers receive persisted data blobs with 1536 dims in downstream stores (affects storage size and retrieval)?
- Should we support variable-dimension rerank inputs in the short term (pad/truncate) or force strict invariant?

Notes-to-self: keep scratchpad chronological. After finishing triage, move polished summary to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/incidents/ with postmortem template.

Slack trace/ref: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCD1234/p1677628800000500
PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4123
Linear ticket: https://linear.app/RED/issue/RED-2312-embeddings-dim-regression
